claims.text: SCCP-generated coherent nanoprecipitates govern high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based plasma-facing materials.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote dislocation transmission in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reduce stress concentrations at sites where cracks can initiate prematurely.
The untreated tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy has conventional grain-boundary and intragranular structures without engineered nanoprecipitates.
Applying SCCP induces a high density of coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy.
The relevant high-temperature testing regime is around 800 °C.
Testing around 800 °C in an environment simulating fusion-plasma exposure represents fusion-reactor service conditions.
The coherent nanoprecipitates are nanometer-scale and uniformly distributed both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Dislocation transmission across coherent precipitate interfaces provides a pathway for stress relaxation.
Reduced local stress concentration suppresses crack initiation and thereby improves high-temperature ductility and fracture toughness.
The SCCP-treated alloy will have higher yield strength at high temperature than the untreated baseline.
The SCCP-treated alloy will sustain greater plastic strain before fracture at high temperature than the untreated baseline.
The SCCP-treated alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the untreated baseline.
Microscopy of the SCCP-treated material will show more uniform dislocation motion and fewer stress-concentration regions than the control.
The untreated baseline has lower high-temperature ductility and toughness and more pronounced stress-concentration regions.
The proposed mechanism should hold for tungsten-based refractory alloys near 800 °C.
Applicability to other material systems or substantially different temperatures is uncertain.
The optimal nanoprecipitate density and size distribution for maximizing ductility and toughness are not established.
Nanoscale dislocation dynamics associated with the proposed mechanism require further confirmation.
